description: Experience the rich and creamy delight of Butter Chicken, a beloved Indian classic. Tender chicken pieces are simmered in a luscious tomato-based gravy, enriched with butter, cream, and aromatic spices. This iconic dish offers a perfect balance of sweet and tangy flavors, making it an irresistible choice for any meal.

instructions.title: Marinate the Chicken
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine chicken pieces with yogurt, 1 tablespoon ginger garlic paste, lemon juice, 1 teaspoon Kashmiri red chili powder, turmeric powder, 1 teaspoon garam masala, and salt. Mix well to coat the chicken evenly. Cover and marinate in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes, or preferably 2-4 hours.

instructions.title: Cook the Chicken
instructions.text: Heat 1 tablespoon of butter in a large pan or skillet over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken in batches, ensuring not to overcrowd the pan. Cook until browned and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes per batch. Remove the cooked chicken and set aside.

instructions.title: Prepare the Gravy Base
instructions.text: In the same pan, melt the remaining 3 tablespoons of butter. Add chopped onions and saute until translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add 1 tablespoon fresh ginger garlic paste, green cardamom pods, cinnamon stick, and bay leaf. Cook for another 2 minutes until fragrant.

instructions.title: Simmer the Tomato Gravy
instructions.text: Stir in crushed tomatoes, 1.5 teaspoon Kashmiri red chili powder, coriander powder, cumin powder, and sugar. Bring to a simmer, then add the soaked cashews. Cover and cook for 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the tomatoes soften and the oil starts to separate.

instructions.title: Blend the Gravy
instructions.text: Remove the whole spices (cardamom, cinnamon, bay leaf) if desired, though they can be blended. Carefully transfer the gravy mixture to a blender and blend until completely smooth. You may need to add a splash of water if it is too thick. Pass the blended gravy through a fine-mesh sieve back into the pan for an extra smooth texture.

instructions.title: Combine and Finish
instructions.text: Return the cooked chicken to the smooth gravy. Stir in the heavy cream and crushed kasuri methi (fenugreek leaves). Simmer for another 5 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the chicken to heat through. Taste and adjust seasoning if necessary.

instructions.title: Serve Hot
instructions.text: Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro. Serve your delicious Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani hot with naan bread, roti, or basmati rice.

tips: For a richer flavor, marinate the chicken overnight. The longer it marinates, the more tender and flavorful it will be.
Soaking cashews before blending is crucial for achieving a smooth, creamy texture in the gravy without any grittiness.
Always finish the Butter Chicken with a good swirl of heavy cream and crushed kasuri methi; these are key for its signature rich taste and aroma.
article:
Butter Chicken, or Murgh Makhani as it's known in its native India, is more than just a dish; it's a global culinary phenomenon. This iconic Indian lunch recipe has captivated palates worldwide with its rich, creamy texture, tantalizing aroma, and perfectly tender chicken. Originating from the bustling streets of Delhi, it’s a dish that evokes comfort, celebration, and a deep appreciation for Indian spices and flavors. If you’ve ever dreamed of recreating that restaurant-quality magic in your own kitchen, you’re in the right place. Get ready to dive into the secrets of crafting an authentic and irresistible Butter Chicken Recipe that will impress even the most discerning foodies.

## What is Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani?

At its heart, Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani is a mild, subtly sweet, and incredibly rich curry featuring succulent pieces of chicken cooked in a velvety tomato-based sauce. The name "Murgh Makhani" literally translates to "chicken with butter," a testament to the generous amounts of butter and cream that contribute to its distinctive luxuriousness. The chicken is typically marinated in yogurt and a blend of spices, then either grilled, roasted, or pan-fried before being simmered in the famous orange-hued gravy.

The story of Butter Chicken begins in the 1950s at the Moti Mahal restaurant in Delhi, where Kundan Lal Gujral is credited with its invention. Looking for a way to use leftover tandoori chicken, he combined it with a fresh tomato puree, butter, and cream, creating a dish that quickly became a sensation. Its widespread appeal lies in its balanced flavor profile – a delightful interplay of tanginess from tomatoes, sweetness from sugar and cream, and a gentle warmth from aromatic spices like cardamom and fenugreek leaves (kasuri methi). It’s a dish that truly embodies comfort food, making it an enduring favorite among Indian lunch recipes and a must-try for anyone looking to master a classic Butter Chicken Recipe.

## Ingredients You'll Need for Butter Chicken

Crafting the perfect Butter Chicken requires a careful selection of ingredients. Here's what you'll need to embark on your Butter Chicken Recipe journey:

For the Chicken Marinade:
*   500g boneless, skinless chicken thighs or breasts, cut into 1-inch pieces
*   1/2 cup plain yogurt
*   1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste
*   1 teaspoon red chili powder (Kashmiri chili powder for color)
*   1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder
*   1 teaspoon garam masala
*   1/2 teaspoon salt

For the Creamy Tomato Gravy:
*   2 tablespoons unsalted butter
*   1 tablespoon oil (vegetable or canola)
*   1 large onion, finely chopped
*   1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste
*   1-2 green chilies, slit (optional, for a hint of heat)
*   1 bay leaf
*   2 green cardamom pods
*   1 cinnamon stick (1-inch piece)
*   1 cup tomato purée (from fresh tomatoes or canned crushed tomatoes)
*   1/4 cup raw cashews (soaked in warm water for 15-20 minutes, then drained) or blanched almonds
*   1 teaspoon red chili powder
*   1 teaspoon coriander powder
*   1/2 teaspoon cumin powder
*   1/2 teaspoon garam masala
*   1/2 teaspoon sugar (or to taste, balances the tanginess)
*   1/2 teaspoon salt (or to taste)
*   1/2 cup water or chicken broth
*   1/4 cup heavy cream (plus extra for garnish)
*   1 teaspoon kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves), crushed

For Garnish:
*   Fresh coriander leaves, chopped

## Step-by-Step Guide to Making Butter Chicken

Following this detailed Butter Chicken Recipe will ensure a delicious outcome.

1.  Marinate the Chicken: In a large bowl, combine the chicken pieces with all the marinade ingredients. Mix well, ensuring each piece is coated. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or ideally 2-4 hours, or even overnight for best results.
2.  Cook the Chicken: Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a large pan or skillet over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken pieces in a single layer, working in batches if necessary to avoid overcrowding the pan. Cook for 5-7 minutes on each side until lightly browned and cooked through. Remove the chicken from the pan and set aside.
3.  Prepare the Gravy Base: In the same pan, melt 2 tablespoons of butter with the remaining 1 tablespoon of oil over medium heat. Add the chopped onions and sauté until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Stir in the ginger-garlic paste, green chilies (if using), bay leaf, cardamom pods, and cinnamon stick. Cook for another 1-2 minutes until fragrant.
4.  Build the Gravy Flavor: Add the tomato purée, soaked cashews (or almonds), red chili powder, coriander powder, cumin powder, and garam masala to the pan. Mix well and cook for 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the mixture thickens and the oil starts to separate from the sides. This step is crucial for developing deep flavors.
5.  Blend the Gravy: Carefully transfer the hot gravy mixture to a blender. Remove the bay leaf, cardamom pods, and cinnamon stick if you prefer a smoother texture, though they can be blended in. Add 1/2 cup of water or chicken broth. Blend until completely smooth and creamy. For an extra velvety texture, you can pass the blended gravy through a fine-mesh sieve back into the pan.
6.  Finish the Gravy: Return the smooth gravy to the pan. Bring it to a gentle simmer over low-medium heat. Stir in the sugar, salt, and crushed kasuri methi. Add the cooked chicken pieces to the gravy.
7.  Add the Cream: Pour in the heavy cream and stir gently. Let the butter chicken simmer for another 5-7 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the chicken to absorb the rich sauce. Taste and adjust seasonings if necessary.
8.  Garnish and Serve: Remove from heat. Garnish with a swirl of extra cream and fresh chopped coriander leaves.

## Pro Tips for the Perfect Murgh Makhani

Achieving that authentic, restaurant-quality taste in your Murgh Makhani is all about a few key details:

*   Marination is Key: The longer you marinate the chicken, the more tender and flavorful it will be. Overnight is ideal.
*   Quality Tomatoes: Use good quality canned crushed tomatoes or blend fresh, ripe tomatoes. The quality of your tomatoes significantly impacts the gravy's flavor.
*   Achieving Smoothness: Blending the gravy base thoroughly until completely smooth is crucial for that signature velvety texture. Straining it afterwards takes it to another level.
*   Don't Skimp on Butter and Cream: While you can reduce them slightly for a "lighter" version, butter and cream are essential to the dish's richness and flavor profile.
*   Kasuri Methi Magic: Dried fenugreek leaves (kasuri methi) are non-negotiable. Crush them between your palms before adding to release their aromatic oils. They provide a unique, slightly bitter, and sweet aroma that defines Butter Chicken.
*   Balancing Sweetness and Tang: Sugar helps balance the tanginess of the tomatoes. Adjust to your preference.
*   Smoking (Dhungaar Technique): For an authentic smoky flavor reminiscent of tandoor-cooked chicken, place a small, heat-proof bowl in the finished curry. Heat a small piece of charcoal until red hot, place it in the bowl, drizzle a teaspoon of ghee over it, and immediately cover the pot for 5-10 minutes.

## Serving Suggestions for Butter Chicken

Butter Chicken is a versatile dish that pairs beautifully with a variety of accompaniments, making it a perfect centerpiece for any Indian lunch recipes spread.

*   Naan Bread: The classic pairing. Warm, fluffy naan is perfect for scooping up every last drop of the rich gravy. Garlic naan or butter naan elevate the experience.
*   Basmati Rice: Steamed basmati rice or fragrant jeera rice (cumin rice) provides a lovely contrast and helps absorb the creamy sauce.
*   Roti or Paratha: Other Indian breads like whole wheat roti or flaky paratha also make excellent dippers.
*   Side Salad: A simple kachumber salad (diced cucumber, tomato, onion with lemon juice) offers a refreshing crunch.
*   Raita: A cooling yogurt-based raita (cucumber or mint) can balance the richness of the curry.
*   Lassi: A sweet or salted yogurt drink (lassi) is a traditional beverage that complements the meal perfectly.

## Variations and Substitutions for Murgh Makhani

While the classic Butter Chicken Recipe is a masterpiece, there are many ways to adapt it to dietary needs or personal preferences:

*   Vegetarian Makhani: Easily convert this into Paneer Makhani by replacing chicken with cubes of paneer (Indian cheese), or Tofu Makhani for a vegan option (ensure no dairy in the marinade or gravy). You can also make a Mixed Vegetable Makhani.
*   Healthier Options: Reduce the amount of butter and cream, or substitute some of the cream with cashew cream or a lighter dairy alternative. You can also bake or grill the chicken instead of pan-frying.
*   Spicier Version: Increase the amount of red chili powder or add extra green chilies to the gravy. A pinch of cayenne pepper can also add more heat.
*   Nut-Free: If you have a nut allergy, you can omit the cashews/almonds and use a teaspoon of poppy seeds or a tablespoon of coconut milk powder (dissolved in water) to achieve a similar richness and thickness.
*   Dairy-Free/Vegan: For a completely dairy-free version, use oil instead of butter, substitute yogurt with a plant-based alternative for marination, and use coconut cream or cashew cream instead of heavy cream. Pair with plant-based chicken substitutes or vegetables.
*   Smoky Flavor Without Charcoal: A pinch of smoked paprika can impart a subtle smoky note if you don't want to use the charcoal method.

Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani is a celebration of flavors and textures, a dish that has earned its place as a beloved culinary icon. With this comprehensive guide, you now have all the tools to create a truly spectacular version in your own kitchen. So, gather your ingredients and try this incredible Butter Chicken Recipe today – your taste buds will thank you!
